items.title: Sonny Igoe interviewed by Monk Rowe, Emerson, New Jersey, July 31, 2003
items.q: But anyway, we all made the same: Charlie Parker, everybody. Twelve bucks.

ctx.x: Yeah. Stick with being a Boy Scout. Well tell me a little about making a living in the studio scene in New York.

Well that was one of the happiest times in my life because I was always home and saw my children, and saw my children grow up. Because I missed so much of my first daughter when I was with Woody. He gave me time to go home for the baby and I had to quit to get the time. And so he had another two or three drummers. I was out of the band for ten weeks. And so our baby was now close to ten weeks old, okay? And I get a call, I thought that I already played with Woody Herman, I already played with Benny Goodman…
